title: Sparkplug session
summary: The engine keeps one session per edge node on a connection, and inside it one metric registry per device ID. Data is accepted only inside a session that began with a birth. The top row is the edge node; the right side is each device behind it.

boxes.label: Waiting for birth
boxes.detail: The engine has no online session for this edge node. Every data packet is refused with "a fresh birth certificate is required".

boxes.label: Session online
boxes.detail: NBIRTH must carry seq 0 and a bdSeq metric (Int64, 0 to 255). The session remembers bdSeq, the last sequence number and a hash of the birth. An identical NBIRTH while online is a duplicate and is ignored, as is a packet that repeats the last sequence number.

boxes.label: Runtime asks for rebirth
boxes.detail: Sent at most once per 30 seconds per edge node; requests inside that window are queued. On reconnecting to the broker the runtime asks every edge node with active devices.

boxes.label: Device not announced
boxes.detail: The edge node is online but has not sent a DBIRTH for this device ID in the current session. The edge node's own metrics use an empty device ID and are registered by the NBIRTH itself.

boxes.label: Device registered
boxes.detail: DBIRTH lists every metric with a unique name, its datatype and optionally a unique alias. Later data may use the alias alone; the engine resolves it and checks the datatype against the birth.

boxes.label: Device offline
boxes.detail: The device's registry is closed and its presence is offline. The edge node's session stays online.

edges.label:
sequence gap, unknown alias or metric,
datatype change, NDEATH, broker lost

steps.text: Data from an edge node with no session is refused. The runtime does not guess: it asks for the births again.
The rebirth request is an NCMD, rate limited to one per 30 seconds per edge node.
NBIRTH with seq 0 and a bdSeq metric starts a session and registers the edge node's own metrics.
Each device behind the edge node announces itself with a DBIRTH: metric names, datatypes and aliases.
DDATA is accepted while its metrics resolve through the birth with the same datatypes.
Every NDATA and DDATA must carry the next sequence number, wrapping at 256. A repeat of the last number is dropped as a duplicate.
DDEATH closes one device. Its presence becomes offline; the session stays online.
A gap, an unknown alias, a changed datatype, an NDEATH that matches bdSeq, or a lost broker connection closes the session. NDEATH means offline; the others mean unknown until the next birth.
